headline: KPMG Buys Into Deepfake Detection. Cybersecurity AI Is the New Practice Area.
summary: KPMG took a stake in Reality Defender, a deepfake detection company, adding AI-generated content detection to its cybersecurity practice. The healthcare-specific use cases are more urgent than they appear: synthetic voice attacks impersonating clinicians, AI-generated telemedicine fraud, and fabricated clinical documentation are near-term attack vectors that most health system security programs have not fully modeled. KPMG is building the capability to advise on this. Firms that do not have a comparable offering will face client questions they cannot fully answer.
so_what: KPMG took a stake in Reality Defender, a deepfake detection company, as part of its cybersecurity push. For healthcare clients, this is a signal that the big four accounting and consulting firms are building AI-specific security capabilities, and deepfake detection in healthcare has a specific use case that most health system security teams have not modeled yet.
original_title: Reality Defender Stake Adds Deepfake Detection to KPMG's Cybersecurity Push
